Question 1 (seats with a job, several seeds), settled with Jack Heart (2026-11-12): "i think the eval expression language should not need to think about seeds. i agree taht we should figure out which games which seeds are playing earlier rather than later so that the eval infrastructure can load things correctly"; then, on the worked example below, "yeah that works". Rule: `games` on a Seating is per point (per position of the job), never per seed. Etude splits a point's games evenly over the subject job's launched seeds (known when its runs launch, before any checkpoint; remainder to the lowest seeds). Each held checkpoint plays its share against its partner: for a seat with a `job`, that job's line with the equal training seed; no equal seed is a gap that says so. Example: w160l8 seeds 1,2,3 vs Aligned(job="w64") with games=1000: seed1 vs w64 seed1 334, seed2 vs seed2 333, seed3 vs seed3 333; the point pools 1000. Launching another seed later changes the split and replays that job's points; docs say so. Replaces "play every line and take the mean" (questions 1 and 9).
